reviewContext.scope: Fresh-context Phase 1c spec review, sprint-3 iteration-3. Independently re-verified iteration-2's single fix (FIND-1003's 2-argument executeLoanIssuanceAttempt call + getCitizen/gojoLogRows wiring) via REAL, fresh live execution against the real, unmodified lending-orchestrator.mjs -- not merely static reading. Then swept broadly, per this iteration's own manifest instructions, for whether the corrected getCitizen closure's own specified contract is genuinely SUFFICIENT for a real Phase-2b implementer working from REQ-117's text alone, and for cumulative internal consistency across all 3 rounds of fixes. REQ-101-116 remain correctly out of scope (already converged sprint-1/sprint-2).

evidence.location: fresh execution this review: `node` against the real, unmodified ~/anicca/skills/economy/lending/lib/lending-orchestrator.mjs, single-argument call `executeLoanIssuanceAttempt({lenderId:'a', borrowerId:'b', nowMs: Date.now()})`
evidence.description: Confirmed the BASELINE crash FIND-1003 identified is genuinely still reproducible against the real, unmodified function when called the OLD, pre-fix way (sanity check before testing the fix itself): threw `TypeError: getCitizen is not a function`, exactly as FIND-1003 documented.

evidence.location: fresh execution this review: `node` against the real, unmodified lending-orchestrator.mjs, 2-argument call `executeLoanIssuanceAttempt({lenderId, borrowerId, nowMs}, {getCitizen, gojoLogRows, ledgerFile, lockStatePath, disburse: stub})` with a getCitizen closure returning full citizen records (id, wallet.evm, walletAddress.evm, coLocatedWithCoordinator, fuel, humanDependencies, AND balanceUsd)
evidence.description: FIND-1003's OWN fix independently re-verified ACCURATE and GENUINE for what it specifically targeted: the corrected 2-argument call shape, exactly as REQ-117's step-6 correction now specifies, completes with zero exception and reaches a genuine `{status:"active", loanId:"loan_lenderA_1"}` outcome (full success path, disburse stubbed). `getCitizenCallCount` was 4 (step 2's pre-lock co-location check + step 6's fresh recheck, for both lender and borrower), confirming the 'fresh per-call, never a stale snapshot' discipline the spec's own correction text claims is genuinely exercised. This closes FIND-1003's own narrowly-targeted crash cleanly -- the crash itself is genuinely gone when a complete citizen record (including balance) is supplied.

evidence.location: fresh execution this review: SAME 2-argument call and SAME fixture roles, but with `getCitizen` returning EXACTLY the literal shape REQ-117's own text specifies (`{id, wallet, walletAddress, coLocatedWithCoordinator, fuel, humanDependencies}` -- no `balanceUsd`, since REQ-117's text never instructs merging one in)
evidence.description: NEW critical finding (FIND-1004), found during this iteration's own broader sweep of whether REQ-117's text is genuinely SUFFICIENT for an implementer, not merely whether FIND-1003's own recommendation was followed. Result: `{status:"refused", reason:"not_broke_enough"}` for a fixture deliberately constructed with one broke and one surplus, otherwise fully-qualifying citizen -- i.e. PROP-117c's own fixture-3 scenario. The REAL `runLockedIssuance` (sprint-2, unmodified) reads `freshBorrower.balanceUsd`/`freshLender.balanceUsd` directly off `getCitizen`'s returned records at its own step-6 fresh recheck, and both consumers (`isBorrowerEligible`, `computeLenderAvailableUsd`) fail CLOSED on a missing balance via `finiteOr` (`Infinity` for the borrower, `0` for the lender) -- a silent, permanent, systematically-wrong refusal, not a crash, defeating REQ-117's own EARS clause ('genuinely INVOKED... when a real eligible candidate exists') just as thoroughly as the original crash did, for the exact scenario PROP-117c's fixture 3 is named to test.

evidence.location: specs/verification-architecture.md line 192 (PROP-117c fixture-3 verification-method, FIND-1003 correction)
evidence.description: PROP-117c's own fixture-3 assertion -- 'a `{status:"active"|"disbursement_failed"|"disbursement_uncertain"|"refused"}` value rather than throwing' -- is confirmed, by this review's own live execution, to be TOO PERMISSIVE to catch FIND-1004: since `"refused"` is one of the four accepted outcomes, a test built exactly to this literal spec text, run against the naive-but-textually-faithful getCitizen closure REQ-117's own shape enumeration invites (no balanceUsd), would report a PASS while the underlying wiring is genuinely, completely broken for its own named scenario. This is a verification-readiness defect distinct from FIND-1003's own (now-closed) crash concern: even a faithfully-implemented PROP-117c fixture 3, run exactly as currently specified, would NOT expose FIND-1004.

evidence.location: specs/behavioral-spec.md lines 2533-2545 (canonical Test-injection seam `deps` enumeration) vs lines 2613-2617 (step-6 correction's own closing sentence)
evidence.description: NEW finding (FIND-1005, major): the step-6 correction's closing sentence references a `deps.getCitizen` OVERRIDE key on `wake-gate.mjs`'s own top-level `runWakeGate` seam as if already established, but the canonical Test-injection seam clause it refers back to enumerates `deps` as covering only `citizensRegistryFile`/`ledgerFile`/`gojoLogFile`/`fetchImpl` -- FOUR keys, none of which is `getCitizen`. This leaves genuinely ambiguous, for a PROP-117c fixture-3 test author, whether `deps.getCitizen` is a real, independent, directly-injectable seam (in which case the canonical enumeration is incomplete) or merely imprecise shorthand (in which case the sentence should not name it as a separate override at all).

convergenceSignals.note: FIND-1003's own fix (round 2) was independently re-verified this iteration via FRESH, real live execution (not merely static reading) and found genuinely accurate and complete for the SPECIFIC crash it targeted -- the 2-argument call shape genuinely prevents `TypeError: getCitizen is not a function` when a complete citizen record (including balance) is supplied. However, this iteration's own manifest explicitly asked for a broader sweep of whether REQ-117's text is genuinely SUFFICIENT for a real implementer working from the text alone, not merely whether FIND-1003's own narrow recommendation was followed -- and that broader sweep surfaced a NEW, critical, previously-undetected defect (FIND-1004): the getCitizen closure's own specified return shape omits `balanceUsd`, which the REAL, unmodified `runLockedIssuance` genuinely requires at its own fresh recheck, and whose absence causes a SILENT, PERMANENT, fail-closed refusal (not a crash) for every real wake -- confirmed by live execution reproducing exactly this outcome against PROP-117c's own fixture-3 scenario. This is the SAME severity class of defect as FIND-1003 (defeats REQ-117's entire reachability purpose) but is HARDER to detect (no crash, no error, exit code 0, indistinguishable from an ordinary no-op wake) and is NOT caught by PROP-117c's own current verification-method text, which permissively accepts `"refused"` as a passing outcome for fixture 3. A related, lower-severity internal inconsistency (FIND-1005) was also found: the step-6 correction's own reference to a `deps.getCitizen` override key is not declared anywhere in the canonical Test-injection seam's own `deps` enumeration. Finding count did not converge to zero and, unlike the prior two iterations, did not even monotonically decrease (1 -> 2) -- this reflects genuinely new discoveries from a broader, more adversarial sweep this round, not regressions in previously-reviewed material (FIND-1001/FIND-1002/FIND-1003's own specific fixes all independently re-confirmed accurate for what they targeted). FAIL -- next iteration required to add the missing `balanceUsd` merge to REQ-117's getCitizen contract, tighten PROP-117c's fixture-3 assertion to reject a `"refused"` outcome for that specific fixture, and resolve the `deps.getCitizen` key ambiguity.
